title: Control board regeneration check with the current shared grid router (diagnostic, not a verification record)
purpose: The delivered control board was generated while grid_router.py had sha256 b78a49cc...; the power-board convergence changed the shared module afterwards. This check regenerates candidate B from the committed generator and placement/plan inputs with the CURRENT module into a scratch directory and compares it with the delivered board. The evidence for the delivered board remains its own kicad-cli DRC manifest (verification/drc/20261011T051246Z-drc-f801ed3c).

geometry_comparison.method: pcbnew 10.0.7: sorted tuples of (net, layer, start, end, width) for tracks, (net, position, diameter, drill) for vias, (reference, position, rotation, layer) for footprints and (net, name, layers, outline vertices) for zones; uuids and timestamps ignored
geometry_comparison.note: The file hashes differ only through uuids/timestamps; every geometric item of the delivered board is reproduced.

without_project_files.note: Artefact of running kicad-cli on a bare .kicad_pcb: 199 lib_footprint_issues warnings (no fp-lib-table) and 12 clearance errors against the KiCad default 0.2 mm rule where the project net class allows 0.15 mm; not a board defect.

with_project_copy.note: Scratch copy of kicad/control_board with the regenerated board swapped in: 0 unconnected, 0 schematic parity, one lib_footprint_issues warning (TerminalBlock_Phoenix library path, footprint J1) that is a copied-path artefact already noted in stored_zone_fill_check.json and absent when the project is checked in place.

conclusion: The control board reproduces geometrically identical with the current grid_router.py (0 unresolved, same counts, project-complete DRC 0 unconnected / 0 parity / no clearance finding); the recorded shared_router_sha256 in routing_progress_control.json refers to the module version at generation time and is superseded by this check for reproducibility purposes.
